messages:
evan: Heads-up: opened a docs PR 3340 to add a small migration note for streaming retries when upgrading from v1 -> v2 SDK. Found a few customers hitting silent drops if they retried mid-page.

tara: link?

evan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3340. The change is mainly explanatory but also adds live code snippets for py/ts/go.

leo: I'll look at the Go snippet. Are we normalizing the cursor name?

evan: We decided in previous threads to highlight language differences but standardize on the concept. Show `resume_token` in py, `resumeToken` in ts, `ResumeCursor` in go. Also include a tiny note about checkpoint frequency.

tara: For the migration note: add an explicit step: "If you previously retried individual items, switch to restart-from-cursor and implement idempotency." It's short but important.

docs-bot: Deploy preview available: https://deploy-preview-3340--docs.redwood.ai

evan: Sample py snippet I added:

```py
async def resume_consume(client, start_token=None):
    token = start_token
    while True:
        page = await client.streaming.read_page(cursor=token)
        async for item in page:
            handle(item)
        token = getattr(page, "resume_token", None)
        if token is None:
            break
        persist(token)
```

leo: Go example LGTM, just a small comment about using context cancellation to avoid leaks.

tara: small wording nit: replace "silent drops" with "partial page loss on retries". I'll push that edit.

evan: Thanks, merging after edits. We'll follow up with a short SDK note for engineers about adding an explicit `resume()` helper in v2.
